### Occupational Health & Safety  
Unilever reported a Total Recordable Frequency Rate (TRFR) of 0.41 recordable work-related accidents per 1 million hours worked in 2025, down from 0.55 in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. This metric covers both employees and non-employees (e.g., contractors), with employee-specific TRFR declining from 0.58 to 0.43 over the same period [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. In 2025, there were 92 total work-related accidents (84 involving employees, 8 involving non-employees), compared to 165 in 2024 (152 employees, 13 non-employees) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. Work-related ill health incidents totalled 2 in 2025, while no figure is provided for 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. Days lost due to injuries, fatalities, and work-related ill health amounted to 1,936 calendar days in 2025, down from 2,946 in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. Unilever’s health and safety management system covered 100% of its workforce in both 2025 and 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. One fatality occurred in 2025 — a contractor at an Ice Cream factory due to workplace violence — prompting a global investigation and implementation of corrective actions across sites [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_137].

### Training  
Unilever delivered mandatory annual Code training to all employees in 2025, including content on recognising bullying and harassment, discrimination, forced labour, working hours policy, and inclusion [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. Additional mandatory training — such as sexual harassment training — was implemented in several countries to meet regulatory requirements [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. In 2025, targeted upskilling initiatives included global Artificial Intelligence (AI) training covering prompt engineering, responsible AI use, and practical applications (e.g., AI-powered menu suggestions, Copilot for financial reporting) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. Social-First training was also rolled out globally to marketers, focusing on insight generation, growth strategy, innovation, and brand-building in culture [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. These programmes were delivered via cross-function ‘learning hours’ and the Workday global learning platform [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127].

### Diversity  
At the top management level (Unilever Leadership Executive and senior management one level below), women constituted 29% (27 of 92 individuals) in 2025, down from 32% (35 of 109) in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_133]. ### GRI 302 Energy  
Unilever’s total energy consumption was 5,224 thousand MWh in 2025, down from 6,482 thousand MWh in 2024 (2024 measured including Ice Cream) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_63]. Fossil sources accounted for 38% of total energy consumption in 2025 (41% in 2024), while renewable sources contributed 62% (59% in 2024) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_63]. Renewable electricity sourcing reached 88% in 2025 (85% in 2024), comprising 85% purchased renewable electricity and 3% on-site self-generation [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_64]. Energy intensity—MWh per € million net revenue—was 103 in 2025, down from 107 in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_64].

### GRI 303 Water  
Total water consumption in Unilever’s own operations was 14 million m³ in 2025, down from 17 million m³ in 2024 (2024 measured including Ice Cream) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_75]. Of this, 9 million m³ was consumed in areas classified as high or extremely high water stress under the WRI Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas (ESRS definition); Unilever’s broader definition—including site-specific review—identified 10 million m³ [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_75]. Water intensity was 272 m³/€ million in 2025, versus 281 m³/€ million in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_75]. Total water recycled and reused was 2 million m³ in both years [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_75]. Unilever does not set formal global targets for water withdrawal in its own operations or upstream value chain; water use is managed via local environmental performance targets and product innovation (e.g., Wonder Wash detergent) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_73].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (market-based) totalled 0.54 MtCO₂e in 2025, up from 0.47 MtCO₂e in 2024, due to reclassification of some on-site, third-party-produced utilities from Scope 2 to Scope 1 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_60]. Gross market-based Scope 2 emissions fell to 0.06 MtCO₂e in 2025 from 0.21 MtCO₂e in 2024 (71% reduction), driven by expanded Energy Attribute Certificate (EAC) procurement [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_58]. Total Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions (market-based) were 97.04 MtCO₂e in 2025, a 11% decrease from 108.65 MtCO₂e in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_58]. Scope 3 emissions in scope of Unilever’s net zero ambition totalled 47.21 MtCO₂e in 2025, down 17% from 56.61 MtCO₂e in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_58]. Near-term SBTi-validated targets include a 100% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 (vs. 2015 baseline) and a 42% reduction in Scope 3 Energy & Industrial (E&I) emissions by 2030 (vs. 2021 baseline) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_48].

### GRI 306 Waste  
Total waste generated in Unilever’s own operations was 493 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 731 thousand tonnes in 2024 (2024 measured including Ice Cream) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Hazardous waste generated totalled 24 thousand tonnes in 2025 (31 thousand tonnes in 2024) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Of this, 19 thousand tonnes (79%) were diverted from disposal; 5 thousand tonnes were directed to disposal (4 thousand tonnes incinerated without energy recovery, 1 thousand tonnes landfilled) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Non-hazardous waste generated was 469 thousand tonnes, of which 467 thousand tonnes (99.6%) were diverted [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Non-recycled waste totalled 114 thousand tonnes (23% of total waste), down from 183 thousand tonnes (25%) in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Unilever’s Climate Transition Action Plan (CTAP), approved by shareholders in 2024, outlines its 2030 climate targets and integrates decarbonisation actions into Business Group strategic planning cycles [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25]. The CTAP supports the long-term net zero ambition by 2039 and incorporates scenario analysis aligned with IPCC pathways (<2°C, <3°C, >4°C) and TNFD-aligned nature scenarios to assess resilience across time horizons [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_30]. The Corporate Responsibility Committee—reporting to the Board—reviews sustainability strategy and tracks progress against climate goals five times per year [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_7]. Key climate-related risks include systemic biodiversity collapse, supply chain disruption from ecosystem degradation, and regulatory exposure from Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_15][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_20]. Core metrics include absolute Scope 1–3 GHG emissions, energy intensity, water intensity, and waste diversion rates—all reported annually against SBTi-validated baselines [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_47].

### Not covered in source material  
No disclosure was found regarding: (1) water withdrawal by source (e.g., municipal, groundwater, surface water) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_74]; (2) detailed breakdown of waste composition by material type [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_99]; (3) quantitative data on refrigerant leak rates or SF₆ emissions beyond methodology descriptions [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_54]; (4) board-level integration of climate risk into enterprise risk management frameworks [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_7].

Scope 3 emissions in scope of Unilever’s net zero ambition totalled 47.21 MtCO₂e in 2025, down 17% from 56.61 MtCO₂e in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_58]. Near-term SBTi-validated targets include a 100% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 (vs. 2015 baseline) and a 42% reduction in Scope 3 Energy & Industrial (E&I) emissions by 2030 (vs. 2021 baseline) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_48].

### GRI 306 Waste  
Total waste generated in Unilever’s own operations was 493 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 731 thousand tonnes in 2024 (2024 measured including Ice Cream) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Hazardous waste generated totalled 24 thousand tonnes in 2025 (31 thousand tonnes in 2024) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Of this, 19 thousand tonnes (79%) were diverted from disposal; 5 thousand tonnes were directed to disposal (4 thousand tonnes incinerated without energy recovery, 1 thousand tonnes landfilled) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Non-hazardous waste generated was 469 thousand tonnes, of which 467 thousand tonnes (99.6%) were diverted [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Non-recycled waste totalled 114 thousand tonnes (23% of total waste), down from 183 thousand tonnes (25%) in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Unilever’s Climate Transition Action Plan (CTAP), approved by shareholders in 2024, outlines its 2030 climate targets and integrates decarbonisation actions into Business Group strategic planning cycles [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25]. The Corporate Responsibility Committee—reporting to the Board—reviews sustainability strategy and tracks progress against climate goals five times per year [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_7]. Key climate-related risks include systemic biodiversity collapse, supply chain disruption from ecosystem degradation, and regulatory exposure from Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_15][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_20]. Core metrics include absolute Scope 1–3 GHG emissions, energy intensity, water intensity, and waste diversion rates—all reported annually against SBTi-validated baselines [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_47].

### Training  
Unilever delivered mandatory annual Code training to all employees in 2025, covering recognition of bullying and harassment, discrimination, forced labour, working hours policy, and inclusion [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. Additional mandatory sexual harassment training was implemented in several countries to meet regulatory requirements [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. In 2025, targeted upskilling initiatives included global Artificial Intelligence (AI) training on prompt engineering, responsible AI use, and practical applications (e.g., AI-powered menu suggestions, Copilot for financial reporting), as well as Social-First training for marketers on insight generation, growth strategy, and brand-building in culture [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. At the top management level (Unilever Leadership Executive and senior management one level below), women constituted 29% (27 of 92 individuals) in 2025, down from 32% (35 of 109) in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_133]. Across the entire workforce, women represented 37% of permanent employees (34,663 of 93,731) and 46% of temporary employees (1,097 of 2,359) as of 31 December 2025 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_131]. Unilever requires business partners to adhere to the Responsible Partner Policy (RPP), which mandates human rights obligations and remediation of negative impacts [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_112]. Business partners confirm compliance annually via self-assessments, due diligence, and risk-based audits; outcomes determine approval status and inform risk-based engagement strategies [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_112]. ### GRI 302 Energy  
Unilever’s total energy consumption was 5,224 thousand MWh in 2025, down from 6,482 thousand MWh in 2024 (2024 measured including Ice Cream) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_63]. Fossil sources accounted for 38% of total energy consumption in 2025 (41% in 2024), while renewable sources contributed 62% (59% in 2024) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_63]. Renewable electricity sourcing reached 88% in 2025 (85% in 2024), comprising 85% purchased renewable electricity and 3% on-site self-generation [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_64]. Energy intensity—MWh per € million net revenue—was 103 in 2025, down from 107 in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_64].

### GRI 303 Water  
Total water consumption in Unilever’s own operations was 14 million m³ in 2025, down from 17 million m³ in 2024 (2024 measured including Ice Cream) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_75]. Of this, 9 million m³ was consumed in areas classified as high or extremely high water stress under the WRI Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas (ESRS definition); Unilever’s broader definition—including site-specific review—identified 10 million m³ [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_75]. Water intensity was 272 m³/€ million in 2025, versus 281 m³/€ million in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_75]. Total water recycled and reused was 2 million m³ in both years [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_75]. Unilever does not set formal global targets for water withdrawal in its own operations or upstream value chain; water use is managed via local environmental performance targets and product innovation (e.g., Wonder Wash detergent) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_73].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (market-based) totalled 0.54 MtCO₂e in 2025, up from 0.47 MtCO₂e in 2024, due to reclassification of some on-site, third-party-produced utilities from Scope 2 to Scope 1 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_60]. Gross market-based Scope 2 emissions fell to 0.06 MtCO₂e in 2025 from 0.21 MtCO₂e in 2024 (71% reduction), driven by expanded Energy Attribute Certificate (EAC) procurement [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_58]. Total Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions (market-based) were 97.04 MtCO₂e in 2025, a 11% decrease from 108.65 MtCO₂e in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_58]. Scope 3 emissions in scope of Unilever’s net zero ambition totalled 47.21 MtCO₂e in 2025, down 17% from 56.61 MtCO₂e in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_58]. Near-term SBTi-validated targets include a 100% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 (vs. 2015 baseline) and a 42% reduction in Scope 3 Energy & Industrial (E&I) emissions by 2030 (vs. 2021 baseline) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_48].

### GRI 306 Waste  
Total waste generated in Unilever’s own operations was 493 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 731 thousand tonnes in 2024 (2024 measured including Ice Cream) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Hazardous waste generated totalled 24 thousand tonnes in 2025 (31 thousand tonnes in 2024) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Of this, 19 thousand tonnes (79%) were diverted from disposal; 5 thousand tonnes were directed to disposal (4 thousand tonnes incinerated without energy recovery, 1 thousand tonnes landfilled) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Non-hazardous waste generated was 469 thousand tonnes, of which 467 thousand tonnes (99.6%) were diverted [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100]. Non-recycled waste totalled 114 thousand tonnes (23% of total waste), down from 183 thousand tonnes (25%) in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_100].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Unilever’s Climate Transition Action Plan (CTAP), approved by shareholders in 2024, outlines its 2030 climate targets and integrates decarbonisation actions into Business Group strategic planning cycles [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25]. The CTAP supports the long-term net zero ambition by 2039 and incorporates scenario analysis aligned with IPCC pathways (<2°C, <3°C, >4°C) and TNFD-aligned nature scenarios to assess resilience across time horizons [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_30]. The Corporate Responsibility Committee—reporting to the Board—reviews sustainability strategy and tracks progress against climate goals five times per year [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_7]. Key climate-related risks include systemic biodiversity collapse, supply chain disruption from ecosystem degradation, and regulatory exposure from Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) schemes [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_15][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_20]. Core metrics include absolute Scope 1–3 GHG emissions, energy intensity, water intensity, and waste diversion rates—all reported annually against SBTi-validated baselines [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_25][unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_47].

### Not covered in source material  
No disclosure was found regarding: (1) water withdrawal by source (e.g., municipal, groundwater, surface water) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_74]; (2) detailed breakdown of waste composition by material type [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_99]; (3) quantitative data on refrigerant leak rates or SF₆ emissions beyond methodology descriptions [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_54]; (4) board-level integration of climate risk into enterprise risk management frameworks [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_7].

### Occupational Health & Safety  
Unilever reported a Total Recordable Frequency Rate (TRFR) of 0.41 recordable work-related accidents per 1 million hours worked in 2025, down from 0.55 in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. The TRFR applies to Unilever’s entire workforce and covers both employees and non-employees (e.g., contractors), with all incidents allocated according to defined methodology — including proportional allocation for shared sites and case-by-case assessment for fatalities [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. In 2025, there were 92 total work-related accidents (84 involving employees, 8 involving non-employees), compared to 165 in 2024 (152 employees, 13 non-employees) [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. Work-related ill health incidents totalled 2 in 2025; no figure is provided for 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. Days lost due to injuries, fatalities, and work-related ill health amounted to 1,936 calendar days in 2025, down from 2,946 in 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. Unilever’s health and safety management system covered 100% of its workforce in both 2025 and 2024 [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136]. One fatality occurred in 2025 — a contractor at an Ice Cream factory due to workplace violence — prompting a global investigation and implementation of corrective actions across sites [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_137]. No TRFR target or forward-looking occupational health and safety goal is disclosed in the source material [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_136].

### Training  
Unilever delivered mandatory annual Code training to all employees in 2025, covering recognition of bullying and harassment, discrimination, forced labour, working hours policy, and inclusion [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. Additional mandatory training — such as sexual harassment training — was implemented in several countries to meet regulatory requirements [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. In 2025, targeted upskilling initiatives included global Artificial Intelligence (AI) training covering prompt engineering, responsible AI use, and practical applications (e.g., AI-powered menu suggestions, Copilot for financial reporting), as well as Social-First training for marketers on insight generation and brand-building in culture [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127]. These programmes were delivered via cross-function ‘learning hours’ and the Workday global learning platform [unilever-sustainability-statement_chunk_127].
